flow.title: Read the denial

features.title: 835 / ERA parsing
features.text: Reads X12 remittance files and separates real denials from patient responsibility.

features.title: Policy retrieval (RAG)
features.text: Indexes payer manuals and returns the exact clauses for the procedure and denial.

features.title: Chart evidence mapping
features.text: Checks each policy criterion against chart sentences and flags what is missing.

features.title: Cited appeal letters
features.text: Drafts with Claude when a key is set, or an offline template. Both cite their sources.

features.title: Win-probability model
features.text: A logistic regression ranks appeals. It learns from your recorded outcomes once you have enough.

features.title: Recovered revenue tracking
features.text: Record each outcome and watch the dashboard add up what was won back.

approach.title: Parse
approach.text: Read the remittance and isolate the denial code, group code, remark and amount.

approach.title: Retrieve
approach.text: TF-IDF search over payer policy chunks with an exact procedure-code boost, optionally blended with semantic embeddings.

approach.title: Extract
approach.text: Tag chart sentences as labs, imaging, exam findings, failed treatments and duration.

approach.title: Check
approach.text: Compare every policy criterion with the best matching chart evidence. Mark it met, partial or missing.

approach.title: Draft
approach.text: Write the letter. Every claim carries a [P#] policy or [E#] evidence reference, and unsupported citations are rejected.

approach.title: Estimate
approach.text: Score the appeal with a transparent model and list what would improve it.

playbook.title: Check the deadline
playbook.text: Most payers allow about 180 days from the denial. Confirm it in your plan documents.

playbook.title: Read the exact reason
playbook.text: Use the denial code and the remark code, not just the summary.

playbook.title: Get the policy
playbook.text: Ask which medical policy was applied and read its criteria.

playbook.title: Collect proof
playbook.text: Dated notes, test results, prior treatments and the physician's rationale.

playbook.title: Write to the criteria
playbook.text: Quote each requirement and point to the matching record.

playbook.title: Ask for a peer-to-peer
playbook.text: For medical-necessity denials, request a call with the payer's medical director.

faq.q: How long do I have to appeal?
faq.a: Often about 180 days, but check your plan. Pramaan AI shows days left and whether the deadline rule is verified.

faq.q: Does Pramaan AI send the appeal for me?
faq.a: No. You review and edit the draft, download the PDF packet and send it yourself.
No. Until real outcomes are recorded they come from a model trained on synthetic data, and the app labels them that way.
Notes stay in this app's database. If you enable the Claude option, identifiers are removed first and only the claim facts used in the letter are sent to the Anthropic API.

faq.q: Is this medical or legal advice?
faq.a: No. It is decision support for billing staff and patients.

about.title: Denials are rarely a medical problem
about.lead: They are usually a documentation problem. Pramaan AI is a third-year minor project at GLA University, Mathura that automates the slowest part of fixing them.
about.name_note: Pramaan is the Hindi word for proof or evidence. It is the one thing an insurer cannot argue with, so every appeal we draft is built around it.

footer.note: Minor project, Department of Computer Science and Applications, GLA University, Mathura. Team 105.
footer.disclaimer: Pramaan AI is a decision-support tool. It does not give legal or medical advice.
